headline: Soft US inflation halves September rate-hike odds, lifts S&P 500 to record
tldr: Fed September hike probability fell from 55% to 34% after both CPI and PPI came in cooler than expected.
S&P 500 hit an all-time intraday high above 7,800; Nikkei and European semis also rallied, though FTSE dipped 0.56%.
Farage won Clacton with 62% of the vote but skipped the count; a parliamentary standards probe into a £5m donation now resumes.
Iran has reaffirmed closure of the Strait of Hormuz, keeping upward pressure on oil prices and UK inflation into Q3.
Brighton's Minteh, Mitoma and Baleba all carry injuries ahead of GW1; Aston Villa's Watkins, Konsa and Martínez also in doubt.

sections.title: Markets
sections.body:
**Markets — Friday 14 August 2026**

The dominant driver is now a double confirmation: both CPI (Wednesday) and PPI came in soft, reinforcing the same disinflationary signal from two angles. 
Both CPI and PPI inflation data for July came in somewhat cooler than expected, pushing expectations for a Fed rate hike in September lower.
 
The probability of a hike at the September 16 FOMC meeting has fallen to around 34%, from roughly 55% last week
 — a meaningful repricing that is doing the heavy lifting across asset classes this morning.

**US** — 
The S&P 500 rose to a fresh all-time intraday high, adding 0.65% and surpassing 7,800 for the first time ever, closing at 7,798.99.
 
The Nasdaq gained 0.81%, boosted by Meta, Micron, and Netflix.
 Oil pulling back helped: 
Brent shed more than 2% to close at $87.07, with WTI settling at $81.25, as traders weighed falling oil demand against the ongoing US-Iran conflict.


**Japan** — 
The Nikkei extended its rally, following Wall Street's lead as subdued US inflation data prompted traders to scale back Fed rate-hike expectations.
 
Tech led — Kioxia, Advantest, and SoftBank all up over 5%.
 IJPN's +0.58% in the pre-fetch is the tail end of that move.

**Europe/FTSE** — The picture is choppier today. 
The FTSE 100 is down 0.56% to 10,772, the DAX -0.12%, and the CAC 40 -0.28%.
 
European equities moved higher earlier in the session as the in-line inflation report strengthened expectations that the Fed could leave rates unchanged in September
, but London's gains evaporated by late morning. The FTSE is now 49 points below yesterday's 10,821 close — the broad defence sector retreat (BAE -1.50%, Rolls-Royce -1.36%) is the visible drag, likely profit-taking after a strong geopolitical-premium run.

**Sam's portfolio:** VUSA (+0.62%) and VEVE (+0.52%) track the US/global relief trade cleanly. ASML's +2.09% is the standout — consistent with 
European semiconductor firms jumping sharply in 2026 as key drivers of the Stoxx 600.
 The defence names are giving back yesterday's gains without a fresh catalyst; WDEF's +0.05% suggests the ETF is holding up better than the individual names on diversification. AMD (+0.02%) is essentially flat — the inflation trade has already been priced into semis this week.

sections.title: Fantasy Premier League
sections.body:
**Deadline: Friday 21 Aug, 17:30 BST — 7 days away**

**Prices**

Prices remain locked until after the GW1 deadline. Nothing to act on here.

**Injuries — what's moved**

Brighton's injury picture has worsened since yesterday's briefing. 
Minteh (leg), Mitoma (hamstring) and Baleba (ankle) are all carrying injuries ahead of their final pre-season fixture against Bologna today.
 No scan result for Minteh has been confirmed publicly yet — Hurzeler is still in "wait and see" mode. 
All three are usually certain starters, which is a worry given Brighton's Conference League first-leg play-off in Norway on 20 August
 — just one day before GW1 kicks off.

The practical FPL consequence: 
[Fantasy Football Scout](https://www.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/2026/08/10/fpl-pre-season-vuskovic-bow-minteh-injury-ndiaye-pen-doubts) notes Gomez (£5.0m) started almost all Brighton matches from GW6 onwards last season, scoring five times — a lack of Minteh and Mitoma makes him very appealing for Brighton's opening four fixtures.


New concern flagged today: 
[Fantasy Football Fix](https://www.fantasyfootballfix.com/blog-index/fpl-gameweek-1-guide/) reports Martínez, Konsa and Watkins were all absent from Aston Villa's Super Cup squad against PSG, making all three doubts for GW1.
 If you hold Watkins (£8.0m), that's now a live concern.

**Differentials — any movement?**

Two new names in circulation today beyond yesterday's Havertz/Tarkowski/Vuskovic thread:

- 
[Fantasy Football Fix](https://www.fantasyfootballfix.com/blog-index/best-fpl-differentials-gameweek-1-2026-27/) highlights **Tavernier** (Bournemouth, £6.0m) — seven goals, four assists last season with 8.63 xG, suggesting he was unlucky not to return more FPL points.

- 
**Schade** (Brentford, £6.0m) also flagged — eight goals, five assists last season, with his highest projected GW1 points coming against Spurs.


**Main action today: Brighton vs Bologna (3pm) — watch whether Gomez starts and whether any Minteh/Mitoma scan news drops before or after.**

sections.title: Data & BI
sections.body:
**Data & BI**

Two new items today, plus a PBIR status update.

**Power BI — TMDL View lands in the Service.** The July update (shipping now) brings 
TMDL View on the web
 alongside Model Options in the Service — meaning you can inspect and edit tabular model definition language directly in the browser without needing Desktop. Also noteworthy: 
from August, semantic model settings open in a new side pane rather than the full settings page, so you can update refresh schedules and credentials without leaving your workspace.
 Minor UX change, but worth flagging if anyone raises "the settings page looks different."

**PBIR default-on — still not confirmed landed.** 
The plan remains to enable PBIR by default in Power BI Desktop in July/August, contingent on a clean service rollout.
 No confirmation it has shipped as of today. Keep checking your Desktop build.

**Semantic layer — AI agents sharpening the use case.** The dominant theme across the analytics engineering community right now is that 
AI analytics failures are more often semantic failures than hallucinations — the model picks the wrong table, joins at the wrong grain, or aggregates incorrectly — and a governed semantic layer prevents the majority of these errors before a query runs.
 Practically, 
dbt Wizard gives analytics engineers an AI agent grounded in their project's lineage, contracts, tests, and metrics, while the dbt MCP server makes the Semantic Layer queryable in natural language.
 If your org is experimenting with AI querying your data, this is the architectural lever — not prompt engineering.

sections.title: Career & Data Leadership
sections.body:
**Director-level salary range: a cleaner number**


Glassdoor puts the UK average for a Data Director at £111,261, with the typical band running £87,293–£142,492.
 That's the step up from the Head of Data figures already covered — useful context for where the trajectory ends. 
Director-level compensation has moved significantly over the past two years, driven by persistent scarcity of commercially credible candidates and increasing scope as C-suite structures are rationalised.
 
Total compensation including bonus and equity at PE-backed businesses will typically be 30–80% above base.


**Market conditions: specialist roles holding, generalist roles softening**


UK job vacancies fell again to around 717,000 in the July–September 2026 period, continuing a multi-year decline.
 But the picture is uneven: 
demand for data architects, engineers, and scientists remains strong and growing, while the market for generalist tech skills will most likely remain flat or see very modest growth.
 The practical implication for a Head of Data candidate: specialism and governance remit matter more than broad seniority.

**The semantic layer is becoming a leadership differentiator**

A concrete signal from [Analytics8](https://www.analytics8.com/blog/ai-and-data-strategy-in-2026-what-leaders-need-to-get-right/): 
analytics leaders should shift effort away from building more outputs and toward fixing the foundations — starting by identifying where critical KPIs are defined differently across teams, then consolidating that logic into shared, governed semantic layers.
 
Once meaning is standardised, self-service and AI finally work the way they were promised to.
 Framing this as a solved problem in interview is a stronger signal than listing tooling deployed.

**Data literacy as a Head of Data mandate, not an HR task**


[The Executive Outlook](https://theexecutiveoutlook.com/blogs/effective-data-leadership-tips-lead-drive-impact-2026) argues the most impactful data leaders treat organisational data literacy as part of their mandate — not generic training programmes, but targeted capability building that helps specific business leaders make specific decisions better.
 That's a reframing worth owning in a leadership narrative.

sections.title: UK Insurance
sections.body:
**Motor: pricing floor reached, losses deepen**

EY's July analysis updated the outlook: 
after a profitable 2024 with a net combined ratio of 98%, the market fell back into the red in 2025 (estimated NCR 102%), with an NCR of 108% now forecast for 2026.
 
The weaker outlook is driven primarily by premium rate reductions since late 2024 feeding through to earned premium. EY expects motor premiums to increase 4% in 2026 and a further 12% in 2027 as insurers respond to persistent claims cost pressure.
 The repricing is already beginning: 
the market is becoming more polarised, with the gap between stronger and weaker-performing insurers widening, reinforced by recent M&A and consolidation.


**Urban Jungle / IKEA: embedded home insurance, FCA Scale-up Unit**

The freshest development this week: 
the FCA's announcement came five days after Urban Jungle's IKEA partnership, launched on 5 August, giving IKEA's UK customers access to a digital-first home insurance platform with contents cover up to £120,000 and buildings cover up to £1 million as standard.
 
Customers can purchase policies digitally within minutes, with monthly rolling terms removing the need for long-term commitments.
 
Urban Jungle has now joined the FCA's Scale-up Unit, with the watchdog promising tailored support to help it innovate, navigate regulation and grow sustainably.
 
It is the only insurtech in the cohort.
 The distribution angle matters for personal lines incumbents: a high-footfall retail brand now sits in the home insurance market with active regulatory backing.

**FCA: pure protection market study due**


The FCA intends to conclude its pure protection market study later in 2026, with an emphasis on closing the "protection gap" and improving awareness and claims experiences
 — worth watching for any cross-sell implications in bundled home/life propositions.

**MK Tech Week — programme detail added**

The week's broader shape is now clearer. 
Alongside the flagship conference, scheduled events include The Open University's conference on the future of adult and lifelong learning in the age of AI, Stadium MK's Stadiums of the Future showcase, and a workshop hosted by the National Committee for Robotics Regulations and Standards.
 
The flagship conference will cover AI, advanced manufacturing, deep technology, and the role of the Oxford-Cambridge Growth Corridor.
 
If you're hosting or attending satellite events, avoid Monday 12 October evening and the full day of Thursday 15 October
 — those are the protected core slots. Speaker announcements are still to come over summer.

Nothing materially new on council or planning decisions since yesterday's briefing. The investment pipeline and housing consultation stories have not moved on.

sections.title: News
sections.body:
**Clacton — Farage wins, skips count.** Result overnight: 
Farage won with 62% of the vote
, though the contest produced its own sideshow. 
He was elected but did not attend the count, claiming Essex Police had warned him of a credible threat and "an organised campaign to disrupt and degrade the result."
 
It is understood no candidates were in fact advised by Essex Police not to attend.
 
Turnout was 44.7%, with 35,401 total votes cast
 — well below the 2024 general election figure, despite Farage's "people vs establishment" framing. 
His return to Parliament means the parliamentary standards investigation into the £5m donation resumes; were he to be suspended for more than 10 sitting days or 14 calendar days, it would trigger a recall petition and a further by-election.
 
Commentators have already derided the whole episode as a "circus", and the questions over Reform's finances remain unresolved.


**Assad sentenced to death.** 
A Syrian court sentenced Assad and his brother to death in absentia for crimes against humanity and war crimes during Syria's 14-year conflict, which left around half a million people dead.
 The ruling is largely symbolic given Assad is in exile, but it adds formal legal weight to the accountability process.

**Hormuz remains shut.** 
The commander of the IRGC Navy has reaffirmed Iran's firm control over the Strait of Hormuz, stressing that the strategic waterway is still closed.
 With no sign of imminent de-escalation, upward pressure on energy prices — and UK inflation — is likely to persist into Q3.
